title: The codegree decomposition conjecture for point configurations
statement:
Let $\boldsymbol{\mathbf{A}}$ be a point configuration of dimension $d$, and let $\operatorname{deg}(\boldsymbol{\mathbf{A}})$ denote its degree. A **codegree decomposition** consists of disjoint nonempty subsets of $\boldsymbol{\mathbf{A}}$ satisfying the face and codegree additivity conditions, and its length is the number of factors.

**Codegree decomposition conjecture.** If

$$
d>2\operatorname{deg}(\boldsymbol{\mathbf{A}}),
$$

then $\boldsymbol{\mathbf{A}}$ admits a codegree decomposition of length at least

$$
d+1-2\operatorname{deg}(\boldsymbol{\mathbf{A}}).
$$

This is a strengthening of the weak Cayley configuration conjecture: a codegree decomposition implies a weak Cayley configuration of the same length. The source presents this as the main structural conjecture, with special cases proved.
source_name: Arnau Padrol, “Neighborly and almost neighborly configurations, and their duals”, arXiv:1304.7186 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.7186

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2013).
